$description: Struct-level golden vectors for postFieldBytes — the post payload inside its creating transaction's TxId preimage (TYPES_INTERFACE -> Layout - Post). The encode direction runs the production writer; the decode direction runs an independent reader written from the layout table, so a vector also proves the preimage is self-delimiting and canonical. A post id is NOT derived from these bytes — it comes from the creating transaction.

vectors.name: post/minimal
vectors.note: 36 bytes: 1 + 0 content, 32 author, 1 count, 1 version, 1 type. The struct's own shape, with every field at its zero value — so the byte COUNT is what this pins, and nothing else can. Content and protocolVersion sit below their protocol minimums; the ENCODER has no such rule, and putting one here would make this file a second statement of a validation rule.

vectors.name: post/golden
vectors.note: 95 bytes, and THE cross-implementation anchor: the demo UI's hand-written mirror is asserted byte-identical to it. Adjacent fields hold distinct non-zero values (author 00..1f, ref 11..), because a transposition of two same-width fields is invisible at zeros.

vectors.name: post/no-refs
vectors.note: post/golden with the ref removed: exactly 32 bytes shorter. A ref costs the 32 raw bytes it names and nothing else — no length prefix, no second hexing — so the delta is the ref itself.

vectors.name: post/wide-numerics
vectors.note: protocolVersion at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER — eight bytes, the top of the encodable number domain. One byte more and readVlqU raises vlq-overflow, which is exactly what keeps the ten-byte all-ones sentinel from ever decoding back into a plausible value. type is enum8, fixed at one byte.

vectors.name: post/multibyte-content
vectors.note: lpUtf8 counts BYTES, not characters: 11 characters encode as 0x12 = 18 bytes. Two refs so the array's count byte is not stuck at 0 or 1 (the ENCODER has no cap — MAX_PARENT_REFS is a validation rule, and putting it inside the writer would be a guard added to compensate for a domain, which the format forbids). type is 'profile' (tag 1) — exercises the non-zero tag.

rejects.name: post/non-minimal-content-length
rejects.note: post/minimal with the content length written as the padded `80 00` instead of `00`. Decodes to a byte-identical value, so steps 1 and 2 both pass and only the re-encode compare separates it.

rejects.name: post/trailing-byte
rejects.note: post/minimal with one byte appended. The struct is fully satisfied before the input runs out — step 2.

rejects.name: post/truncated-author
rejects.note: Empty content and then 19 of the author's 32 bytes. Wire's own rejection, not a boundary-check one: a fixed-width read that runs off the end.

rejects.name: post/unknown-type-tag
rejects.note: post/minimal with the type byte set to 0x02 — an unassigned tag. enum8 refuses an unknown tag rather than decoding it to a neighbour.

rejects.name: post/type-sentinel
rejects.note: post/minimal with the type byte set to 0xff — the encode-side sentinel. It must not decode back into a value, so the sentinel is unreachable from a well-formed post.
